extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners solving classical geometry and elementary mechanics problems (mathematical enthusiasts, 19th-century problem-solvers)
extracted.subtask_description: Deriving analytic or geometric solutions to plane geometry and elementary mechanics exercises: define variables and geometry, apply calculus/trigonometry or statics/dynamics principles, and produce algebraic or constructed results (often with multiple solution methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: State geometry and variables explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Let labelled points, lengths, angles, and axes be defined at the start of the solution (e.g. 'Let Q be the point in which the vertical axis meets the horizontal plane and O the centre of the cylinder's base', 'Assume OA = a, height = h, QO = c').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always introduce notation for points, distances, angles, masses, densities, axes, and origins; draw or refer to a diagram. This is used repeatedly across solutions as the first step; omission leads to confusion. Examples: definitions of OA, a, h, QO = c in the cylinder problem; AB, A, a, h in beam problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conservation of energy (vis viva) when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the equation of vis viva (conservation of kinetic + potential energy) to relate radial motion and rotation (e.g. 'the equation of vis viva gives ...' for the spiral wire and ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly write the energy equation, substitute expressions for velocities, and integrate or rearrange to obtain motion laws. Useful for problems with rotating/revolving masses where energy exchange is central. Anti-pattern: using only force-balance when energy conservation is the simpler route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take moments (torque) about a convenient point/line for equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate equilibrium by taking moments of forces about a chosen pivot or line (e.g. 'taking the moment of each elemental centrifugal moving force about this line', 'taking the moments of the forces keeping AB in equilibrium about B').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a pivot that eliminates unknown reaction forces when possible. Integrate elemental moments for continuous bodies or sum for point loads. This appears in many rigid-body statics solutions (beam against wall, cylinder about AP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decompose forces and exploit symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve centrifugal, gravitational, or tension forces into components and use symmetry to cancel opposing components (e.g. 'the components ... y are pw^ydxdydz; but since the latter forces ... destroy each other two and two, it is clear that the centrifugal force will tend to turn the cylinder about a line AP').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify components that integrate to zero over symmetric bodies to reduce the problem (cancel pairs two and two). Use resultant force through centre of gravity when possible (e.g. resultant of centrifugal forces equals M·ω^2·... through mass centre).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use small-angle / small-quantity approximations for oscillations
rubrics_metrics.description: For small oscillations or small angles, linearize trigonometric functions and neglect higher-order terms (e.g. 'for small oscillations, the tension of each string will be ... the resolved part ... nearly equal to ...'; 'since r → a, we have ... which gives position at time t').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the smallness assumption explicitly and use linear approximations (sin θ ≈ θ, cos ≈ 1) to reduce differential equations to simple harmonic form. Show resulting period or time of oscillation. Anti-pattern: applying linear formulas without justifying smallness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose coordinate systems and perform integrals for distributed bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce rectangular or polar axes and integrate elementally for kinetic energy, moments, or mass distributions (e.g. plate rotated by strings: introduce (r cos φ, r sin φ, 0) and integrate over plate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take origin at convenient centre (often centre of gravity), express elemental mass dm and kinematic quantities, then integrate over region. Keep track of limits and use symmetry to simplify integrals. This is required for continuous-body problems (circular plate, cylinder moments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use center-of-gravity / resultant-force arguments to replace detailed integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace distributed-force integrals by resultant acting at the centre of gravity when symmetry allows (e.g. 'The resultant of the centrifugal force of all the particles is horizontal and passes through the centre of gravity ... Take the moment of this force and of the weight').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the resultant of distributed forces is known and passes through the cg, take moments of the resultant and weight about an axis to get equilibrium relations. Saves substantial computation compared to full integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multiple solution approaches and compare them
rubrics_metrics.description: Present alternative (First, Second, Third ...) solutions using different techniques (geometry, algebra, energy, moments), and show their equivalence (e.g. multiple solutions to beam and horizon problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering several methods demonstrates deeper understanding and can produce shorter/clearer derivations. When giving alternatives, show how forms reduce to the same final expression. It is treated as a mark of neatness and thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use trigonometric identities and right-triangle relations carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive relations between distances and angles via right triangles, cot/cosec relations and identities (e.g. 'AE = AB cot E', 'tan(d+0) = ...', 'sin cos ...' manipulations in beam problems and horizon problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up right triangles in diagrams, write cot/cosec relations, and manipulate to isolate desired quantities. Check algebraic transformations and signs; reduce to simpler trig forms where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze extremum problems via calculus and admissibility of roots
rubrics_metrics.description: For maxima/minima, form the function, differentiate (sometimes differentiate the logarithm), set derivative zero, find real roots, and check which root yields admissible maxima/minima under constraints (e.g. 'Equate the differential coefficient of the logarithm of (I) to zero', 'Since v and w positive ... determine which root gives maximum').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly handle sign and domain restrictions; use theory of equations to determine number/nature of real roots; reject roots that violate positivity or constraint conditions. State conclusions about existence/non-existence of minima/maxima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform numeric computation steps when solving applied examples
rubrics_metrics.description: When numerical data are requested, carry out computation with logs or numeric evaluation and show intermediate values (e.g. computation for mountain horizon using log h, cot α etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include log tables or numeric approximations and show substitution into final formula to compute D and d. Show rounding and units. Anti-pattern: give final numeric answer without showing intermediate computations or units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use geometric construction steps explicitly for synthetic problems
rubrics_metrics.description: For construction problems, give a step-by-step geometric recipe using perpendiculars, bisectors, equal segments, and intersections (e.g. constructions for centre of gravity of quadrilateral, drawing lines from two points to meet a given line making equal angles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each construction move and justify why it yields the required property (e.g., show that a constructed point G is the centre of gravity because of proportional equalities). Provide a diagram reference. Present variations for 'opposite segments' vs 'same segment' cases when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and transform final expressions to known/alternative forms
rubrics_metrics.description: After obtaining a result, transform algebraically to alternate but equivalent forms to match problem statement or known results (e.g. 'This, however, can readily be transformed into the expression obtained in the previous solutions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify algebraic equivalence by manipulating trig identities or factoring; present the most convenient or symmetric form. Use limiting cases to verify correctness (e.g., consider h small in banking problem).
